bug_semantics: phpseclib Net_SSH2/_get_binary_packet() and later SSH2::get_binary_packet() compared a received SSH MAC/HMAC against the locally computed tag with PHP != (and, after 2019, the same != on the UMAC branch). On equal-length binary strings PHP dispatches to memcmp(), which short-circuits on the first differing byte (CWE-208). Every non-AEAD post-KEX packet hits this path; a mismatch disconnects, so the leak is one sample per connection against a fresh session key and is Low/defense-in-depth rather than a practical remote oracle.
flaw_origin: The variable-time MAC compare was first written when SSH2.php was added as a new file in git df0fe2386a66e8b9625d254df5488bdf8f172149 (SVN trunk@4, 2007-07-23). Original sink phpseclib/Net/SSH2.php:1058 in _get_binary_packet(): if ($hmac != $this->hmac_check->hmac(pack('NNCa*', $seq, $packet_length, $padding_length, $payload . $padding))). Later commits only renamed hmac() to hash(), swapped $seq for $this->get_seq_no, and split a UMAC branch; they did not first-write the != mechanism. Immediate parent 367ddebf805eb0071eb4b9deb3abf7e16866c040 (SVN trunk@3 initial commit) has phpseclib/Net/SSH1.php only and no SSH2.php or hmac !=.
